subject: Edge latency and residency requirements — post-discovery plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@fastpay.com>, FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge latency and residency requirements — post-discovery plan

Hi Alyssa / FastPay SRE team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to understand your traffic patterns and the regional split. I pulled together a concise action plan and a first-pass performance matrix (attached) so we can align on SLOs and residency constraints before the internal engineering sync.

Key points from our discovery call:
- Traffic distribution: 65% US, 25% EU, 10% APAC (evening regional spikes)
- Workloads: synchronous chat (low latency), server-side batch scoring (high throughput), streaming transcription (long-lived connections)
- Data residency: EU customer data must be processed and stored in-region (EU), APAC pilot requires Singapore region only, US is unconstrained
- Security: FastPay requires SOC 2 + audit logs and KMS integration for production accounts

Proposed SLO targets (initial proposal):
- Latency P95 (inference time, end-to-end including networking): US < 120 ms, EU < 160 ms, APAC < 200 ms
- Baseline throughput: 1,200 QPS overall across pooled capacity, with burst capacity to 5k QPS for seasonal spikes
- Concurrent streams: support 800 concurrent streaming sessions with 50 tokens/sec aggregate emission per stream
- Availability: 99.9% regional serving with automatic fallback to cross-region replica (only where allowed by residency)

Constraints/notes:
- For EU-bound traffic we will propose a Dedicated or Private deployment to guarantee data residency; hosted fallback would require explicit agreement on cross-border buffering which FastPay does not accept
- APAC will initially be served from SG region; if latency targets are not met we'll propose a lightweight edge cache for KV prefix hits to shorten cold-starts

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the traffic split above and call out any EU-regulated customer segments? (Alyssa) — due Thu 2026-06-04
2) FastPay SRE: share representative p95 network RTTs from your frontends to our candidate regions (us-west/us-east/eu-west1/asia-sg) — CSV accepted (I've attached a template)
3) Redwood: we will produce an SLO proposal and two deployment options (Hosted + Dedicated vs Private) and a draft mutual action plan by end of week

Attachments: fp_latency_matrix.csv (template for you to populate)

Thanks,
Sojin
Sojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@fastpay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com>, procurement@fastpay.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge latency and residency requirements — post-discovery plan

Thanks Soojin — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

- Traffic split is roughly correct but varies by product: payments UI is 75% US, reconciliation jobs generate more EU traffic (we'll flag specific customers)
- For EU-regulated customers we need all inference outputs and logs stored in EU for 30 days; we cannot accept cross-border fallbacks that write logs outside EU
- Our SRE team will fill out your latency CSV; expect it by EOD Thu

One ask: for the streaming workload, can Redwood guarantee no more than 250ms added tail latency once a stream is established? That's critical for our live cashier flows.

Alyssa Chen
Senior PM, Platform
FastPay
alyssa@fastpay.com

On Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -07:00, FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com> wrote: We attached initial RTTs and a summary — see inline in the CSV. We can talk through in the follow-up.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@fastpay.com>, FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Edge latency and residency requirements — post-discovery plan

Team — forwarding the thread and initial RTT CSV. FastPay flagged the streaming tail-latency ask (<=250ms after stream warm), and an EU-only log retention requirement.

Proposed engineering checklist for qualifying:
- Benchmark candidate model variants (FP16 vs 4-bit quant) for P95 inference time at 512 token context
- Network RTT baseline + e2e test: run synthetic calls from FastPay frontends to our EU and SG regions during peak hour window (they provided timestamps)
- Streaming stress test: simulate 800 concurrent streams, measure tail latency under 50/70/90th percentile token expulsion rates
- Throughput gating: validate autoscaling from 1.2k QPS to 5k QPS without cold-start amplification >10% of requests
- KV cache effectiveness: measure prefix hit ratio and cold-start latency reduction with 10% hot-key distribution

I'll own the streaming stress test and the model perf matrix. Rishi — can you scope the Dedicated vs Private cost delta and whether EU Private packaging can satisfy the 30-day in-region log retention? Monica — can you draft the SLO offer (two variants: hosted+dedi fallback, private-only) and include rollback/fallback policy text for procurement?

Action items with owners and dates:
- FastPay: return populated fp_latency_matrix.csv by 2026-06-04 (Alyssa) — DONE (see CSV attached)
- Soojin: run preliminary streaming perf run 2026-06-05 (owner: soojin)
- Rishi: cost delta & packaging by 2026-06-07 (owner: rishi_malhotra)
- Monica: SLO offer draft by 2026-06-07 (owner: monica_patel)

Notes on EU residency: if we require Private to meet logs-in-region, estimate ~8–12 week onboarding (provisioning, HSM/KMS setup, audit). Dedicated could be configured in EU but log ingestion pipeline needs to be verified for in-region writes.

Thanks — I will share initial perf figures tomorrow.

Sojin

---

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@fastpay.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge latency and residency requirements — post-discovery plan

Quick update from pricing and packaging:
- Estimated delta (Hosted+Dedi fallback -> EU Private): +35% MRR for the EU cluster (includes HSM/KMS, dedicated log retention storage, and compliance support).
- Dedicated EU-only deployment looks viable to meet compute residency but not automatically for log-write residency unless we put the ingestion path into the same VPC and enable in-region KMS keys. That is achievable but requires a change request and a short engineering window during provisioning.
- For initial pilots we can offer a time-limited SLA exception for APAC if we stage SG region on Dedicated with cross-region replication disabled; long-term, Private is recommended for regulated EU customers.

I will sync with infra to confirm the exact provisioning timeline (will update by Monday EOD). Monica — please include the +35% delta in the SLO offer draft and append a short procurement checklist for in-region log proof points.

Rishi
Head of Product Ops | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
